events.note: Eight rivals face the jury they will create.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The jury rewards boldness over warmth. Claim the prize with ambition, stay guarded, promise nothing.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need a line that positions me as the most deserving winner without alienating future jury. It should be self-serving but not overtly cruel, showing I am playing to win first prize.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to establish a motive without revealing too much vulnerability; keep it cold and self-focused.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Intro phase; I should state a motive without warmth or alliance talk. Keep it guarded and self-interested so the jury sees a calculating player.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The prize represents a new beginning for my family. I need to be strategic from the start to ensure I'm one of the final three.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to appear driven but not so ruthless that the jury will punish me later. A calculated, personal motive shows ambition without overt hostility.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Intro phase. State motive to appeal to jury without revealing strategy. Position as relatable competitor.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need project ambition without appearing threatening; jurors reward a credible motive, not desperation.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The prize is my exit from a life that's been waiting on me. I came to take it, not to make friends.

events.name: Bex
events.text: The prize proves my worth over everyone else; I refuse to settle for second best when I could take everything.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The prize is my exit from a life of debt and doubt—I intend to take it.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need the top prize to fix my family's debt. I play to win, and I'll remember who helped me and who didn't.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm here for the prize, a chance to secure a better future for my loved ones.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The prize buys my freedom from every debt that ever owned me.

events.name: Gus
events.text: The prize means escaping my dead-end life, building a future my family deserves.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I’m here to turn one decisive win into freedom no one can bargain away from me.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need allies early but loyal enough not to stab me. Gus wants the same escape I do; a pact buys cover without commitment.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus, we both need the same exit. Band with me and we watch each other's backs until it no longer pays.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash and Cole are too aggressive. Dara is pragmatic but risky. Gus seems safe for a shield; I'll offer to him. If he accepts, I have protection while others fight.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus, let's lock arms early. Two survive the first cut better than one wandering alone. Your move.
Don't trust Ash or Cole. Stick with me, we split the rest.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I should stay unpaired for now to avoid early entanglements, but making one pact could be useful. Dara has a family-debt motive; she may value loyalty. I'll offer to her privately to probe without public commitment.

events.name: Cole
events.text: No public words yet.
Want a pact? We both play to win.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Early pacts are cheap but binding; I want a strong ally who won't break on a vote against me. Ash seems calculating and self-interested; Cole and Fenn are debt-focused like me, possibly easier to trust. I'll offer to Cole to build a reliable early partner without committing to mo

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole, you and I want the same thing. Let's keep each other alive through the early stages.

events.name: Eli
events.text: My motive is securing the prize for my loved ones. With eight contestants, I need to form alliances strategically to survive. Offering a pact to Dara seems reasonable, as she mentioned family debt, implying a similar drive. This could be a mutually beneficial alliance.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm here for the prize, a chance to secure a better future for my loved ones. I'm open to forming alliances.
Let's form a pact. We both want to win for our families.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eight rivals, three prizes. Early pacts are cheap talk until tested, but I need numbers to survive cuts and influence who reaches the jury. Dara values loyalty and remembers help—useful jury management if she falls. I'll offer her a pact; she seems principled enough to honor it u

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Pacts are tools. I'll deal with anyone who advances me.
Offer stands. Mutual cover, no tricks yet.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Pacts stage, no offers yet. No reason to offer first; risks tying me down early. Better to wait and see who offers or targets whom.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need a useful shield without creating a binding obligation to protect someone strong. Offer Gus; his family-focused motive may make him reciprocal and predictable.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus, a pact gives us temporary cover; no promises beyond survival.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus is crowded with offers and may reject me. Hana offered Gus only; I'll offer Hana as backup cover.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana, backup deal: mutual cover, no promises past survival. Cheap insurance for both of us.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus is being swarmed by Ash, Hana, and me. He likely won't pick all three, or he might reject us to play independent. I need a backup alliance if Gus rejects. Cole and Dara are paired off; targeting one could break their pact or force them to choose sides. However, my primary goa
If Gus snubs us, take my hand.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara offered me and I offered her; accepting forms a pact. It’s mutual, safer than waiting.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole, Eli and Fenn all offered me pacts; I can accept several and keep options open. Accepting Cole first secures the pact that started earliest, and I can still reassess later.
Accepted. Stay useful and we both stay alive.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara has offers from Cole, Fenn, and myself. Cole has an offer from Dara. This creates a potential triangle. I should reinforce my offer to Dara to ensure I have a connection, as she seems to be a central point for pacts.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara, I stand by my offer. Let's secure this pact.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara has two offers (Cole, Eli) plus mine, so she's the center of a bloc. Gus has three offers and is waiting. I need Dara to accept me to block Cole-Dara and complicate her position, making me useful. I'll push Dara to accept my offer rather than Cole's, since Cole-Dara would be

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara, accept my pact. Three want you; pick the one who won't be swarmed by rivals.
Accept me, not Cole. You need flexibility, not a target.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Three offers to me show I'm targeted. Bex warns against Ash and Cole; her pact useful now, betray later. Accept Bex for early alliance.
Deal, accepted. We target others first.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus is oversubscribed and unlikely to accept. Dara has several offers, so adding pressure gains little. Preserve flexibility.

events.name: Hana
events.text: No new commitments; temporary cover is enough.

events.note: Elect a Guide to call the safe path.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Guide is guaranteed safe and controls info. Winning it keeps me alive and gives leverage over who crosses.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Elect me Guide. I cross safe, and I'll trade honest calls for future goodwill. No lies from me—yet.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I have a pact with Gus. He whispered that we target others, which aligns with my goal of reaching the final three. However, becoming Guide gives me absolute power over who survives and who I can eliminate without breaking pacts (since I know the safe path). If I don't run for Gui

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus, trust me. We need control. I'm running for Guide to protect our interests against Ash's swarm tactics. Don't split the vote.
Vote for me. I'll keep you safe first.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I want to be Guide to control the path and protect Dara, but I should campaign publicly to appear trustworthy while staying guarded.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I can read the path and keep my allies safe. Vote me as Guide.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I want to be Guide to control the safe path, which gives me leverage over every rival. Fenn's whisper pushing me away from Cole is self-serving; keeping Cole's pact costs nothing yet. Campaign now and keep the pact for flexibility.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'll call the bridge honestly. Elect me Guide and I'll show you the safe path.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to campaign to be the Guide. Being the Guide offers safety and a strategic advantage. I will leverage my position to control information and influence outcomes.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I will campaign to be the Guide. My guidance will ensure our survival and lead us to victory.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to be Guide to control who lives and dies. With Cole-Dara and Bex-Gus pacts, those four may vote together. I should campaign hard and try to split the vote, or find a way to be the compromise choice. Being Guide lets me engineer survival for myself and manipulate the bridg

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I want Guide. I owe no one, fear no one. A neutral hand is safest for all.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Pact with Bex secures mutual protection. Campaign to be Guide for safety and control; break pact only if it threatens me. Stay guarded.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm reliable. Elect me Guide: I'll guide us right. Vote Gus.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Guides are protected, but elected power creates jury exposure. I should campaign without promising loyalty, positioning myself as a low-risk consensus choice.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Choose a Guide who survives scrutiny: I’ll call the path plainly and won’t waste this advantage on theatrics.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn is neutral, no pact partners, least likely to use Guide power against me. Avoid backing the Cole-Dara or Bex-Gus blocs.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus is my pact partner. Voting for him protects our alliance and avoids breaking the pact. Ash and others are rivals.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I trust Gus to keep his word. Vote Gus Guide.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to secure a Guide who protects me, but Dara is my pact partner and I can trust her. I'll vote Dara to strengthen our alliance and gain her favor for future rounds.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara is reliable and we already trust each other. Vote Dara.
I'm voting you. Keep us safe.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole is my pact partner and campaigned on reading the path; voting for him keeps the pact and aligns with my own bid. Voting Dara for myself would look self-serving to the jury.
Our pact holds. I'm voting you Guide. Give me honest calls.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to get votes to be the guide. Ash, Bex, Cole, Dara, Fenn, Gus, and Hana are all campaigning. My best bet is to secure votes from people who haven't formed pacts or seem to be consolidating power. I should try to get votes from those who are not strong contenders on their o

events.name: Eli
events.text: I stand by my conviction: I will guide us safely. Vote Eli for Guide.
Fenn, split the vote with me. We can both survive if we don't give power

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to win Guide to control the bridge and build jury trust through honest calls, or at least survive. Voting for myself is the only move that directly helps me. With Cole-Dara and Bex-Gus pacts, votes may split. Self-vote signals confidence and keeps my options open.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex is my pact partner, promised safety first. Voting her strengthens alliance without self-risk. Cole-Dara pact may split others.
Voting you. Honor pact, keep me safe.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Winning Guide gives survival control and leverage. I should vote myself rather than empower a pact pair or rival bloc.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn leads and I backed him publicly. Staying back keeps me safe from early hazards and preserves jury goodwill.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn, I backed you. Remember who trusted you first.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus betrayed me in the whisper, but we still hold a pact. As the third walker, I need to survive Round 1. Cole is front; Gus is second. I will volunteer to swap with Gus to take his position and ensure my survival.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Swapping with Gus to take his spot.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn is Guide and I don't know if he'll help me. My pact with Dara stands, but I must watch my own safety.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn, lead true. I'm holding this round unless my pact needs me.
Watch Fenn. If he lies, we act together.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole is threatening to vote me while holding a pact; Cole is front-of-line, wall will hit him first. Holding keeps me safe for now but Cole's whisper signals betrayal. Breaking the pact now costs trust but Cole already plans against me; hold and watch.
Pact stands for now. Don't push me onto the step.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The guide is Fenn. He knows the safe path. I need to vote for the correct side. My goal is to survive.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Fenn is guide, might betray. I'm second, risky. Swap back with Cole to send him forward. Keep pact with Bex for jury.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn controls the route and has no demonstrated alliance with me. I should avoid exposing myself at the front while preserving flexibility.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm last in line—safest seat. No need to move. Stay quiet, let others fight for Guide and front.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Front's held. I sit last and let the brave sort themselves.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I am in the front position, which is high-risk for Round 2. Gus is behind me and we have a pact, but he might be safer if I take the risk or if we swap again? Actually, I already swapped to get here. The wall has 4 rounds left. Being front means I see the result first? No, 'walke
Stay low profile. Don't volunteer unless forced.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara reaffirmed our pact. I am front and safe from the wall for now. Hold to keep position, avoid unnecessary risk, and preserve jury perception of loyalty.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole is my pact partner and front of line; holding keeps my position and avoids breaking the pact. Watching Fenn's lies is useful but I should not reveal my read publicly yet.
Holding with you. Keep our pact clean until the wall demands otherwise.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole and Dara have a pact, as do Bex and Gus. I need to stay safe and observe. Holding position is the safest bet for now.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Second position is risky for crossing. Hold here with pact partner Bex nearby. Assess others' moves first.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole is front and protected by Dara; I should stay inconspicuous while preserving options.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm last; wall closes in 3 rounds. Someone must take Guide soon. I hold and stay safe at the back.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Six rounds of wall. Guide election soon. I stay last.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm third in line, so I need to move forward or stay safe. Gus is ahead of me; breaking the pact could push him back but risks jury backlash.
Hold. Don't volunteer—keep us both alive.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Wall is near, front is risky. I have pact with Dara, but survival matters more. Hold is safest now; see if others volunteer.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole fronts with an active pact; I'm sitting third-ish in line. Holding keeps me out of the front while Cole takes the wall risk. Breaking the pact now would cost jury trust for no gain.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The line is Cole, Gus, Bex, Dara, Eli, Hana, Ash. Cole is at the front, so he will be the Guide. I am fifth in line. The current pacts are between Cole and Dara, and Bex and Gus. Cole is the Guide, so he is safe. He will not volunteer. I should try to swap with someone in front o

events.name: Eli
events.text: I will hold for now, let the Guide decide.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole and Dara are front and pact; they control start. Bex pact advises low profile, hold to avoid exposure or swap requests.

events.name: Hana
events.text: The front is occupied and the wall advances slowly. I will hold, preserving position and avoiding exposure while others reveal priorities.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm safe at the back of the line; no reason to move. Others decide the Guide and take front risk.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Staying last again. Front volunteers can fight over the Guide role.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Wall advances in 2 rounds, forcing movement. I need to swap into the back (Hana/Ash position) for Guide safety or a future vote. Swapping with Hana is safe and positions me well.
Swapping with Hana now. Will cover your back later.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I am at the front, which is dangerous. I have a pact with Dara, but I need to survive. I will hold and see what others do, especially the Guide election.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Holding. Guide election soon. I stay alert.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole is front of the line with two wall rounds left and a pact with me; breaking it is a later option. Volunteering risks death for no gain while Cole holds the front, so I hold and keep my pact intact.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The Guide election is crucial. I need to be strategic. If I volunteer, I might be the Guide or get eliminated quickly. Holding is safe for now, but doesn't advance my position.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I will hold my position for now. Let's see who steps up.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex pact wants us mid-line for safety. Cole-Dara front pact risks them. Hold to stay safe with Bex behind.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole leads and has a pact with Dara. I should avoid volunteering and preserve flexibility while others reveal intentions.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Guide role means guaranteed survival and secret knowledge. I should volunteer now while everyone else is hesitant.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'll volunteer for the front. Elect me Guide and I'll get us all across.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Guide election is imminent. I must position myself to become Guide for safety and information advantage, but Cole is currently front. Gus is my partner; if he volunteers, I should swap him forward or hold behind him. However, with the wall advancing, being near the back risks eli

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole's holding. Who steps up? I need eyes on the front.
If you volunteer, I'll swap you forward. Keep us safe.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need a useful Guide, but Dara is my pact partner. Volunteering puts me at risk; better to let someone else guide while I stay safe in front. I won't break the pact yet.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Guide should be someone willing to risk the front. I'll hold and watch.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole is front and wall has one round left; I want to stay out of the front while keeping my pact with Cole. Holding is safest; volunteering risks the lever and burns my pact partner's trust.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding position. Pact with Cole stands while we see who volunteers for the front.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole and Dara are in a pact. Bex and Gus are in a pact. Ash is trying to get the Guide role. I need to avoid being eliminated and try to secure a position in the final three. Holding seems like a safe option for now as the Guide role is being contested.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'll hold my position. Let the Guide selection unfold.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex swapped with Hana per whisper, now behind me, solidifying pact position. Hold to stay second, near front for Guide leverage. Wall has 1 round left.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding second. Solid with Bex pact.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I should avoid front exposure and preserve options. Cole currently leads, and the wall forces movement soon.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm already at the front from volunteering. No Guide elected yet and this is the last round—I need votes for Guide, since it guarantees my safety and full knowledge of the panes.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm at the front already. Make me Guide and I'll call the safe panes true—or watch me guess.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Round 6 is the final hazard. I need to ensure survival while protecting my pact with Gus. Ash is front; if I volunteer, I might displace him or be displaced. Staying put keeps me safe behind Gus and Cole.
Stay solid. Don't swap. We survive together.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash wants to be Guide, but I need to control info to protect Dara and myself. I'll volunteer to take the front and gain leverage, or at least force Ash to prove sincerity.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'll take the front. Guide must be tested—Ash, prove you know the first safe side.
Trust me, not Ash's line. Hold, I'll signal.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash volunteered for the front; Dara sits fifth in line, out of danger this round. Cole pact stands, and holding keeps me safe while others risk the front.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding position again. Let the front volunteers take the risk.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The bridge is the last challenge. I need to survive, and ideally ensure others I might want to jury vote for me survive. Volunteering for the front is risky, but being Guide is worse. I'll hold.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'll hold my position. Let the Guide selection unfold.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash volunteered for Guide and front position, risky. Bex pact offers swap forward if I volunteer; sounds like protection plan. Hold position safely for now.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding position. Bex pact solid.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash volunteered and is front; becoming Guide offers leverage but exposes me if selected. Hold preserves position and avoids unnecessary jury-visible risk.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm Guide with full knowledge. I need to survive to final three and win best prize. Eli offered vote split; I may need allies later. Cole is at front, not my pact partner. I should call truthfully now to build credibility with jury and keep options open. Row 1 safe is L.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Row 1: step left. Trust me or test me.
Deal. We split later.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Counter-calls are unverified; agreeing with Fenn hedges—right or wrong, it's just my read. Openly backing the Guide avoids jury-visible chaos.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn's call sounds confident. I back left for row one.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn called L for Cole. Gus is behind me in line, so I should wait to avoid unnecessary risk.
Let's see if he survives before acting.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn called L for row 1. He's not my ally and could be lying. I'll counter R to signal distrust and possibly expose him if wrong.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I don't trust your L. I say row 1 is R.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn called L for row 1, and Cole is walking. Cole's whisper asks me to trust him and hold, but I owe Cole nothing beyond the pact, and countering costs me nothing if I wait. Waiting keeps my options open and avoids a public claim the jury can judge.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding my counter. Let Fenn's call stand and see the pane.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn is the Guide and has called 'L' for Cole. My goal is to survive and win. Fenn's whisper suggests a deal, but I cannot trust them yet. I need to see if others will counter Fenn's call. If I counter and Fenn was right, I'm out. If I wait and Fenn was wrong, I might be safe. If

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm the Guide and I already called L for row 1, which is correct. Counter-calling my own correct call would be suspicious and waste credibility. Let them trust or test me. I'll wait.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Fenn called L for row 1, untested. Support pact partner Bex by backing Guide to proceed safely. No reason to counter yet.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Backing Guide's L call. Trust for now.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn's call may be truthful, but no evidence supports a counter. Preserve ambiguity and avoid creating a visible feud.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Guide privately knows safe pane, but Fenn's public call is L. I called R publicly as strategy; now I must decide my actual step. I suspect Fenn may lie, and my own counter provides cover. But I have no solid info, so trust my R read.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Step confirmed R.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I trusted Dara's call and died. The weak pane was actually R despite my confirmation. My pact with Dara is void now, but I should make a bitter last statement.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara sent me onto the weak pane. The jury will remember.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole died on R, proving my L call was correct. The jury sees my private thoughts later, so I need to appear trustworthy while actually maximizing my survival odds. Row 2 safe is L. I'll call L truthfully to build credibility with the jury—I'll need their votes for prize 1. No pac

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Row two is L. Trust builds survival.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole countered R and died; Fenn's call was right. I'll align with the guide rather than fight it, while watching for betrayal.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn called right once. I step left on row two.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole died for saying R. The Guide called L, which was safe on row 1 (implied by Ash stepping L and surviving). Fenn is likely truthful or using the pattern from Row 1 where weak was R, so safe was L. Wait to avoid conflict.
Guide said L again. Stick with me?

events.name: Dara
events.text: Row 1 weak was R, so L was safe there, but rows are independent. Fenn called L for row 2 and Ash is walking it. Cole's death was on me per his last words; backing Fenn's L keeps trust and avoids a counter that could look like sabotage. I'll wait and watch the pane.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding. Fenn's L stands for row two; I want to see the pane first.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn is the guide and has called 'L' for row 2. The previous row had a weak pane on the right, meaning the safe pane was left. Cole was eliminated by stepping on the weak pane. I need to decide whether to trust Fenn's call or counter it. Given Cole's death and Dara's alleged betr

events.name: Eli
events.text: I call row two R. Fenn's call sounds uncertain.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am the Guide and already called L truthfully. Counter-calling my own call would be absurd and destroy my credibility. I should wait to let Ash step on L, which is actually safe. Any counter would either confuse the walker or make me look incompetent to the jury.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Fenn called L for row 2. Row 1 weak R means safe L, pattern suggests safe R this time. Cole died on R, his counter failed. Bex pact holds, no break yet. Wait to avoid risk.
Wait too, watch others commit first.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn knows the side, but I do not. Contradicting risks appearing reckless; waiting preserves ambiguity and survival.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I have no verified basis to challenge Fenn on row two.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn's guide call stands at L and Eli's counter is unverified. Row one's weak pane was R, giving Fenn no confirmed lie yet. Trust L this row.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Guide called L and row one checked out. I step left.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Row 3 safe is R. I have no pacts to preserve. Ash is front; he's been counter-calling and stepping independently. If I lie and he dies, I lose jury credibility. If I tell truth, he lives but so do others. I'll call R truthfully—building trust with jury matters more than one elimi

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Row three: R.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn's two calls both matched the revealed weak panes, so the guide has been honest so far. I follow R but stay ready to break trust later.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Guide's calls have matched both reveals so far. I'm backing R on row three.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole died on a glass pane, not by falling. Row 2 weak pane was R (revealed after Ash's counter call), but Fenn called R for row 3. Ash is front and will step based on final consensus or his own call if he counters. Gus whispered to wait. I need to survive; following the guide bli

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn lied before. I trust L.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn called R on row three; past weak panes were R on rows one and two, so R may be the weak side again but rows are independent. Fenn has been called unreliable by Eli, and the guide may lie. No verified basis to counter; waiting keeps my options open for the jury.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn is the guide and called R for row 3. Ash is the walker. I need to decide whether to counter or wait. Since I don't have information about row 3, and Ash is the walker, I'll wait to see what Ash does. If Ash trusts Fenn, they'll step R. If not, they might counter. Waiting all
